experimental: B-frames: opt-in with V4L2_VA_B_FRAMES, one B per P. The firmware holds each queued picture until the next one arrives, so the client must keep three pictures in flight (FFmpeg -async_depth 3); with its default two the session stalls at the first pair boundary. The intra period is rounded to a whole number of (P, B) groups, without which the firmware's IDR lands inside a pair and the stream is corrupt from that IDR on. Gate: 300 frames of 720p H.264, 45.06 dB mean PSNR, B pictures present (TEST-RESULTS.md).

codecs.import_note: an alt-ref access unit decodes as two pictures, so the session lends one picture one buffer per completion (the same client buffer queued twice). Chrome destroys a VP9 surface as soon as it has composited the frame, often while the picture is still with the firmware: on 2026-11-11 that released 564 of 768 queueings and dropped 541 completions. The session now retains such a target and completes it (`target detached`), and the 2026-11-12 gates qualified Import: 48/48 four-codec matrix, FFmpeg 1280x720 alt-ref clip 515/515 with framemd5 equal to the software decode, and two guarded Chrome 156 windows at submitted=1705 completed=1705 drops=0 retained=1161 and submitted=1588 completed=1588 drops=0; the Copy baseline over the same clip and window dropped 3 of 1705. TEST-RESULTS.md records each run

codecs.film_grain_note: Synthesis is qualified for AV1Profile0 at 8 and 10 bits. The client names the ungrained decode target as current_frame and a separate grained current_display_picture; the driver decodes the rebuilt access unit with apply_grain=0 and blends in userspace (src/va/grain.cc) from that picture's endPicture, before the client can recycle current_frame. The 2026-11-14 gate resolved the 320x240 NV12 20-frame and 352x290 P010 2-frame clips frame-by-frame identical to libdav1d's grained output under V4L2_VA_PUBLISH=import, and both clips matched under direct and copy as well. TEST-RESULTS.md records the run
codecs.sync_note: The default internal eight-slot DPB translator submits each AV1 picture at vaEndPicture; it assigns refresh slots itself and rewrites ref_frame_idx[] to those slot numbers, so no held picture or successor is needed. When all eight slots are still referenced, the previous uncommitted picture is replayed as a hidden NOSHOW frame in the same temporal unit before the shown frame; the two completions share one token. The first NOSHOW half is invisible and consumes one Import buffer without publishing pixels; the second half is the client picture and publishes even when its own show_frame=0 makes both halves NOSHOW. Target::invisible counts the consumed first half, and a NOSHOW LAST marker at a resolution-change boundary is consumed as invisible rather than failing a token. A client show_frame=0 picture is submitted immediately with no client pixels to publish. A new key frame clears internal slot identities and EOS has no held tail. The firmware returns hidden pictures without pixels; the session attributes them by token or decode order. Import lends one client DMA-BUF per completion, including the invisible half; a completion that lands in a neighbour's buffer fails both surfaces. The installed-package gates for this default path passed on 2026-11-11 on the 0001-0004 module: four-codec matrix 48/48 exact under V4L2_VA_PUBLISH=import, real 1280x720 AV1 clip 120/120 exact framemd5 with 120 publish=import, 42 publish=invisible and 0 errors/drops, and the 1280x720->854x480 in-context DRC clip 80/80 exact framemd5 with 84 completions (42 import, 42 copy-gpu after the DRC switch, 63 invisible). Firefox 158 local AV1 and live YouTube/Bilibili AV1 now report hardware decode with frame/drop windows and no held-picture error; Chrome 156 reports VaapiVideoDecoder with kIsPlatformVideoDecoder=true on both live sites. TEST-RESULTS.md records each run
codecs.resolution_note: A resolution change inside one VA context is supported: CAPTURE must be streaming before the rebuilt pool is queued, because the kernel clears its DRC boundary sub-state (DRC | DRC_LAST) only in iris_process_streamon_output and completes an earlier CAPTURE QBUF as an empty LAST, after which vb2 returns -EPIPE for every later DQBUF. enter_streaming() streams first for both Mmap and Import memories. A client that keeps exporting surfaces at the old CAPTURE geometry cannot receive the new geometry through Import: the 2026-11-10 DRC trace records 'import rejected: client layout differs from the CAPTURE layout' (client stride=1280 size=1413120, capture stride=896 size=647168), configures an Mmap pool and publishes the second half with copy-gpu. Keeping the Import pool would write 896-pitch pixels into a 1280-pitch client buffer; the GPU copy is the fail-safe path, and test/iris-clip-trace-check.sh requires the recorded reason before accepting those copies. Framemd5 on 2026-10-24: 2 of 6 runs passed before the change, 44 of 44 after; the boundary access unit returns a second time as 0x4009 (KEYFRAME, real pixels). TEST-RESULTS.md records the run
